A thousand thanks to Mother Mary and the Holy Son. We are a family living in Melbourne for the past 20 years. My name is Kurian. My wife is Swapna. Our eldest daughter is Nella,
second daughter is Bella, and the third one is Ella. This is George. We are here to share a testimony about how our second daughter
Bella had a cardiac arrest and then a brain impact, and how, through the intercession of Mother Mary to Holy Son, she was healed.
A thousand thanks to Mother Mary and the Holy Son for giving us this opportunity to stand here at this holy altar. On October
17, 2023, at around 1 am, my daughter, who was sleeping at night, fell from the bed to the floor. It was a cardiac arrest.
We didn’t know what had happened. When we went near her and called her, she was almost in a dead condition. There was only a faint heartbeat. That was the situation.
Immediately, we started giving CPR as best as we knew. The child showed no movement. Her lips were turning
pale white. Right then, we called the ambulance. The ambulance staff instructed us to continue CPR, but it didn’t help.
Then, four ambulances arrived—two emergency ambulances and two intensive care ambulances.
All of them together gave CPR to the child for about one and a half hours. In the end, after one and a half hours, they said they didn’t see any major improvement.
With only a faint heartbeat, they decided to take her to RCH, one of the biggest children’s hospitals in the Southern Hemisphere.
They told me that I should come along to say the last goodbye to my daughter. I said I wouldn’t come, but they insisted that I had to come to say goodbye. I was then about eight…
months pregnant. I couldn’t accept this at all because among all of us at home, she was the healthiest child.
Even when everyone got a fever, she never got one. When everyone caught chickenpox, she didn’t. For such a child to suddenly have a cardiac arrest and be in that condition—it was impossible to believe.
My husband went with the ambulance commander to the hospital. When they reached there, the doctors said that Bella’s chances of survival were very low.
They performed open-heart surgery on her and connected her to a machine called ECMO—something we had never even heard of before. Through that, and with the ventilator, her life was being sustained.
They said they would keep her like that for 72 hours, and only after that would they know whether she could be saved or not, and in what condition she might be.
The next day, I went to the hospital with my other children to see her. She looked like a lifeless child—her body covered in tubes everywhere.
We are a family that prays well, but we had only heard about Kreupasanam. We had never taken any covenant or made any such commitment there.
That’s when two priests came to the ICU to administer the Anointing of the Sick (Last Rites).
Along with them came a few trustees and leaders from our church. One of them handed me a bag containing the covenant items and papers.
I couldn’t even understand what it was at that time because of the situation we were in. I just kept it there
in the ICU itself. That bag was given to me by my friend Ramya, who had earlier come here and shared her testimony.
Ramya called me the next day and asked, “Have you started using the covenant items? You must use them.”
Following Ramya’s instructions, I began to anoint my child’s forehead with the blessed oil and apply the blessed salt—doing all those things.
After that, Ramya herself came to see me and told me even more things. She took the rosary from her own neck and put it on mine, even giving me with the covenant medal.
We started praying the Apparition Prayer and used the blessed candle and all. However, we didn’t take the covenant yet.
We were doubtful—how could we follow all the conditions mentioned in it in our current situation? Could we even go for confession every two weeks? We weren’t sure.
Then one day, a large team of doctors called us and said that all of our child’s…
They said brain damage had occurred — all the cells were damaged. “You may get your child back,” they said, “but she will have no
abilities. She will remain completely disabled. She won’t be able to hear. She won’t respond. She will have to live her whole life supported by tubes.”
That was the situation they described. We can’t even fully express here what we went through at that time. I was fully
pregnant then, and with our other children to take care of, I truly don’t know how we made it through those days.
But one thing I can say is this — when we began using all the covenant items, even though our minds were breaking down completely, we started feeling a strange strength within us.
Still, there were moments when, humanly, we would grow weak and lose hope. During that time, the doctors decided to remove Bella from the ECMO machine.
After removing her from ECMO, she stayed in the ICU for two more weeks. But still, there was no change — no brain functions at all.
Then she was moved to the cardiology ward. It was there that we began to see what brain damage really meant.
The child would suddenly slide off the bed, as if falling. She would move like a snake twisting on the floor, lying on the bed and writhing.
It was because the muscles in her body — from her head to her toes — would tighten violently every few minutes. The
pain was so intense that she would rub her hands, legs, and jaw against the bed, until blood stains appeared all over it.
In that state, we continued praying, constantly reciting the Apparition Prayer and pleading with Mother Mary.
Even though we hadn’t yet taken the covenant, we prayed, “Mother, please help the doctors find the right combination of medicines for our child. Only then will she find some healing or relief from this terrible pain.”
We prayed that somehow, through a divine intervention, the doctors would be able to find the correct mixture of medicines for our
child. The doctors who were treating her were among the most experienced — a team of senior consultants, many around 70 years old.
They continued monitoring her closely. After two or three days — or rather, after about a week — they finally said they had found the right combination of medicines for Bella.
However, even with that, there were no visible improvements. Her life was just being sustained — nothing more.
